summary: NautilusCommerce: multipath backpressure causing duplicate streaming completions and increased tail latency — remediation & customer communications
description:
Issue summary: Between ~2026-03-12T12:05Z and 2026-03-12T13:48Z NautilusCommerce experienced duplicate streaming completions and elevated tail latency for conversational traffic routed to multiple backend paths. Impact: multiple customer endpoints observed duplicate partial completions (2x) and long-tail completion latency spikes up to 18s, causing client timeouts and increased token counts billed. Environment: prod us-west serving cluster with mixed quantized and FP model variants. Request pattern: high concurrency with short streaming sessions.

Immediate impact: transactions failing client-side and increased billed tokens observed by customer. This ticket documents the incident timeline, investigation notes, resolution steps, customer-facing communications, and follow-up actions to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send concurrent streaming chat requests from 30+ client connections pinning model redwood-chat-v2-7B with early-response prompts (short prompts, expect streaming).
2) Observe that streaming proxy routes fan out to two backend workers when the primary path reports transient backpressure.
3) Under sustained concurrency, KV cache eviction and incomplete response handoff cause a second completion to be emitted for in-flight request, leading to duplicate partial transcripts.
4) Client libraries that retry on perceived incomplete streams can re-emit, amplifying duplicates.

timeline: 2026-03-12T12:05Z - First customer report via support channel: intermittent duplicate chunks in streaming responses (Nautilus monitoring alerted).
2026-03-12T12:10Z - Triage: Support opened incident, paged SRE and Serving on-call. Assigned Sev1.
2026-03-12T12:18Z - Mitigation: Applied temporary routing policy to disable multipath fanout for Nautilus project. Immediate reduction in duplicates observed.
2026-03-12T12:35Z - Investigations: SRE observed KV cache eviction thrashing on several worker hosts and pathB experiencing degraded kernel selection.
2026-03-12T12:50Z - Rollback: Rolled back recent kernel-switch rollout (PR#1870) that coincided with capacity change. Metrics stabilized.
2026-03-12T13:10Z - Customer update: Nautilus confirmed reduced duplicates; asked for root cause and billing impact.
2026-03-12T13:48Z - Incident declared resolved after 1 hour 43 minutes; monitoring continued for 24h.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Multipath fanout combined with transient backpressure allowed in-flight requests to be retried on alternate path while primary was still delivering, producing duplicate completions.

Hypothesis B: A recent kernel-selection rollout increased per-token latency for the quantized variant on a subset of hosts, triggering the proxy to consider that path degraded and fanout to alternate hosts.
Confirmed: Correlation found between PR#1870 kernel-selection changes and the start of anomalies on 6 hosts in us-west-2. KV cache eviction rate was 3x normal on those hosts during the spike.
No evidence of prompt-level client duplication from Nautilus side; duplicates originate in server path handoff.
customer_communication: 2026-03-12T12:12Z - Support -> Nautilus: Acknowledge receipt, opening major incident, working with SRE; asked for sample request IDs.
2026-03-12T13:15Z - Support -> Nautilus: Provided mitigation steps taken (multipath disabled) and suggested retry-window configuration to reduce client-side replays.

2026-03-13T09:00Z - Follow-up email: Detailed root cause summary and offer of billing credit for duplicated tokens while incident active. Nautilus requested full token accounting and proposed credit amount; finance loop opened.
resolution: 1) Immediate mitigation: Disabled multipath fanout for Nautilus project to prevent parallel in-flight routing until kernel-selection rollback completed.
2) Rollback: Reverted PR#1870 kernel-selection changes on affected host pool which restored expected latency characteristics for quantized model variants.
3) Monitoring: Added targeted synthetic streaming tests and a health-check that validates single-path completion semantics under load.
4) Customer remediation: Offered token credit and produced per-request token accounting for the incident window (shared 2026-03-13).
follow_up_actions: Action 1 - Engineering: Rework multipath handoff protocol to ensure idempotent streaming completions (ticket INT-8921 assigned; target: 2026-04-15).
Action 2 - Runtime: Add guardrail to prevent fanout if backend reports KV eviction rate > threshold (owner: serving-runtime team).
Action 3 - Release process: Add pre-rollout loadstep for kernel-selection changes that runs streaming synthetic for top-10 customers (owner: release-engineering).
Action 4 - Support/CS: Produce a customer-facing FAQ describing behavior and recommended client retry semantics for streaming SDKs.
Action 5 - Billing: Reconcile token accounting and issue credit per Nautilus request; track outcome in SUP-734211.
